instantiated_cells.justification: Executive branch agencies file a separate statement under §13.695 identifying officers/employees engaged in legislative activity rather than registering as lobbyists/principals, and §13.621(2) exempts them from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68.

Elective state officials acting in official capacity are not subject to registration under §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, or 13.695; agencies (including the Governor's office staff) instead file §13.695 statements.

Independent agencies fall within the §13.62(2) definition of "agency" and file §13.695 statements rather than registering as lobbyists; §13.621(2) exempts them from the lobbyist registration provisions.
Lobbying of an agency official by an agency official of a different agency or another agency official of the same agency is completely exempt from the subchapter, so no registration is required.
Employees of the legislature acting in an official capacity are not subject to §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68 or 13.695, and the §13.62(2) "agency" definition excludes legislative councils/committees.

The statute regulates individual "lobbyists" (who are licensed) and "principals" (who register); a lobbying firm itself is not separately defined as a registrant—only the individual lobbyists are licensed and any principal employing them registers.

Local governments are not within the §13.62(2) "agency" exemption and §13.625(4m)(e) expressly references "a principal that is a local governmental unit," indicating local governments can be principals subject to §13.64 registration when they exceed the $500 threshold.
Lobbyists must obtain a license from the commission under §13.63(1)(a), and §13.66 prohibits engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65.
Every principal who makes expenditures or incurs obligations exceeding $500 in a calendar year for non-exempt lobbying must file a registration statement with the commission within 10 days.

"Principal" under §13.62(12) means any person who employs a lobbyist, with no exemption for public entities outside state government agencies (which are exempted under §13.621(2)/§13.695), so other public entities must register under §13.64 when exceeding the $500 threshold.

A "lobbyist" is defined as an individual employed by a principal or who contracts for/receives economic consideration other than reimbursement for actual expenses; unpaid volunteers do not meet this definition and thus need not be licensed.
